title: Enthalpy of combustion of ethanol from a spirit burner
stem: A student heated water in a copper can using a spirit burner containing ethanol, C₂H₅OH (M = 46.08 g mol⁻¹). The literature value for the standard enthalpy of combustion of ethanol is −1367 kJ mol⁻¹. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹.

data.caption: Results of the spirit-burner experiment
rows: Mass of water in can / g

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the heat absorbed by the water, in kJ.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the enthalpy change of combustion of ethanol, in kJ mol⁻¹, from these results.
parts.notes: Apply ECF from (a). Accept −640 to −650 kJ mol⁻¹.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the percentage error of the experimental value compared with the literature value.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Suggest two reasons for the difference from the literature value, and one improvement to the method.
markscheme: heat lost to the surroundings / air / not all heat transferred to the water
incomplete combustion of ethanol (soot on the can)
heat absorbed by the copper can not included / ethanol evaporated from the wick (mass loss not all due to combustion)
improvement: shield the flame from draughts / use a lid and insulation / reduce distance between flame and can / use a bomb calorimeter / supply more oxygen
parts.notes: Award [2] max for reasons and [1] for a relevant improvement. Reject vague answers such as 'human error'.
